request: The PDP needs a CTA for B2B catering orders, and keep PII out of the logs. It belongs under Feature #60 (Catering).

exchanges.say: Your request has four abbreviations to pin down before anything else: PDP, CTA, B2B, and PII. PDP is the riskiest: this app has no product pages, only product tiles on the menu (component:ProductTile), and orders go through POST /api/orders (route:/api/orders). It also names no outcome yet.

questions.ask: PDP usually means product detail page, but this app has no product pages: products show as tiles on the menu (component:ProductTile). Which page do you mean?
questions.default: The menu, since that is where products show today.

questions.ask: B2B can mean orders from companies, or a separate portal for business customers. Which one?
questions.default: Orders from companies through the same app, because a portal is a much bigger build.

questions.ask: By CTA you mean one call-to-action button that starts a catering order?
And PII: the personal data a catering form collects, such as names, emails, and phone numbers?

answers.text: By PDP I mean the menu, /menu, where each product has its tile. We don't have separate product pages.
B2B means offices that order trays of pastries for meetings. Not a separate portal.
Yes, a call to action: one button that starts a catering order.
PII is personal data: customer names, emails, and phone numbers. None of it may show up in any of our logs: the server's logs or the analytics events.

exchanges.say: So: the menu, one call-to-action button, offices ordering for meetings, and names, emails, and phones as the personal data. Now who it is for and what success looks like.

questions.ask: Who places these orders, and for how many people?
questions.default: Office managers ordering for a meeting.

questions.ask: What changes when this works, and how would we know? Orders already go through POST /api/orders (route:/api/orders).
questions.default: Every catering request arrives as an order, counted per week.

questions.ask: What is the smallest version an office manager could try: one button and a short request form, no prices?
questions.default: One button and a short form that sends the request as an order.

questions.ask: Is keeping PII out of the logs part of this story, or its own story?
questions.default: Part of this one, limited to the form's data.

questions.ask: What is out: prices, invoices, company accounts, delivery?

answers.text: Office managers ordering for a meeting of 10 or more people.
Office orders come by phone today and get lost. Every catering request should arrive as an order we can see. I'd like 5 a week through the form to start.
Just an 'Order for your office' button on the menu page and a short form: company, name, email, phone, date, and how many people. It sends us the request as an order; no prices or invoices yet.
Keeping PII out of the logs is part of this: no customer name, email, or phone number may show up in any of our logs, the server's or the analytics events, whatever page or order it came from.
No prices, invoices, company accounts, or delivery.

exchanges.say: Here is what done looks like. Goal: office managers send catering requests through the menu instead of phoning, so none get lost; measured as catering requests received through the form, met at 5 a week. Done when: the menu page shows one "Order for your office" button; it opens a form for company, name, email, phone, date, and people; sending it creates 1 order holding those; and the app logs hold 0 lines with the seeded name, email, or phone. Terms: PDP is the menu, CTA is that one button, B2B is offices ordering for meetings, PII is names, emails, and phone numbers. Prices, invoices, company accounts, and delivery are out.
